statement: TrendForce reports DRAM supply will remain tight through 2027, limiting the wafer capacity memory suppliers can allocate to HBM production, which together with 12-Hi HBM4e validation uncertainty has prompted NVIDIA to assess four alternative HBM specifications for Rubin Ultra since Q3 2026.
why: When the lead accelerator vendor evaluates downgraded memory options because wafer capacity for HBM is short, memory has become the binding constraint on how many full-specification accelerators can ship.

impact.mechanism: Tight DRAM wafer capacity caps HBM output, forcing the GPU vendor toward lower stack heights and slower interfaces, which limits shippable high-end accelerator supply.

evidence.excerpt: DRAM supply will remain tight through 2027
limit the wafer capacity that memory suppliers can allocate to HBM production

confidence.basis: Research-house supply-chain checks, not an NVIDIA statement; the document notes NVIDIA has not confirmed a spec change. Corroborated by the SemiAnalysis relay but that is two publishers, short of three.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 2 -> 3; sources: Lookonchain (summarizing SemiAnalysis), TrendForce
